facts.fact: Niger's communication minister and his Algerian counterpart chaired the official ceremony launching operation of the trans-Saharan fibre backbone linking Niger to Algeria at Assamaka on 6 October 2026, per ANP.

Niger's communication minister arrived in Agadez on 5 October 2026 with Algeria's ambassador and a technical delegation for what the ministry calls the launch of works on the Niger-Algeria fibre optic interconnection; the page is dated 6 October 2026.

facts.fact: Niger's communication minister carried out provisional reception on 14 November 2025 of the Niger component of the trans-Saharan fibre backbone: 1,031 km on five axes to the Algerian, Chadian, Nigerian, Beninese and Burkinabe borders, laid by the LORYNE group with AfDB support; the minister spoke of commercial interconnection with Algeria, Chad, Nigeria and Benin as coming soon.

systems.owner: Niger government, financed by the African Development Bank

facts.fact: ANP reports that works on the trans-Saharan fibre backbone, a NEPAD project launched in 2017 to link Algeria, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria and Chad, actually began in 2021, financed at about 30 billion CFA francs by the AfDB, the African Development Fund and national counterpart funds.

The project coordinator said on 14 November 2025 that all fibre sections on the five axes to Algeria, Chad, Nigeria, Benin and Burkina Faso (1,031 km) were 100 percent built and ready for reception, and the minister held provisional reception; he described technical and soon commercial interconnection with Algeria, Chad, Nigeria and Benin as the final stage.

Niger's and Chad's communications ministers signed a memorandum of understanding on updating and implementing the cross-border interconnection of the Trans-Saharan Fibre Optic Backbone (DTS/FO), and instructed Nigertelecoms and Safitel Chad to open technical talks (ANP report; its body gives a mistaken July date, the dateline reads 19 June 2025).

The ministers reported Niger's civil works at 97% with 48 km of fibre left to reach the Chad border, and Chad's DTS/FO component at 42.78% with Safitel's cable already at the Niger border; interconnection was expected at the end of August 2025.

systems.owner: Niger and Chad governments; operators Nigertelecoms and Safitel Chad

facts.fact: Maroc Telecom's 5,700 km transafrican terrestrial cable from Morocco to Niger via Mauritania, Mali and Burkina Faso is recorded as completed (2020-2022, about US$100 million), connecting the landlocked Moov Africa subsidiaries including Niger's to international bandwidth; the record gives 2022 and publication year 2022 stands as the date.
